guest.bio_context: Jason Benetti grew up in Chicago and began his broadcasting career at Syracuse University's student radio station in 2003, where his first on-air lead-in was the NPR News with Carl Castle. He has a mild case of cerebral palsy, which prevented him from marching with the tuba in his high school band, leading his band director to put him behind a microphone to announce the band's set. He later broadcast the Chicago White Sox for many years before moving to the Detroit Tigers, and in 2026 became the play-by-play voice of Sunday Night Baseball on NBC.

pending_qa.q: How does Lilly King describe the mental pressure of competing at Olympic trials in swimming?
pending_qa.r: King described Olympic trials as uniquely high-pressure because the entire point of the meet is to finish in the top two in your event in order to make the Olympic team. With typically 100 to 150 people competing in a single event, she said the mindset going into the final is simply: 'don't mess up.' She confirmed she did get nervous, despite always expecting to win.

pending_qa.q: Did Lilly King engage in trash talk with competitors before races?
pending_qa.r: King confirmed she did talk trash to opponents before races, noting that her competitors did not appreciate it. She acknowledged that in one Olympic final, refusing to make eye contact with another swimmer off a turn was about as close as trash talk gets while actually in the water.
